description:

I'm confused by this.  You are fetching the 4-byte value above.  But the file is already BASE_HEX, so why are you slicing it down to 2 bytes (4 hex digits) and showing it like this (still in hex)?

What if the value was > 0xffff ?

The same applies to key_kecode below.

Why not just call proto_tree_add_item()?

worth adding and using a true_false_string for this (and others?) field?

The field is called "down-flag" and I'm not sure what text values could "fit" into it.
https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#qemu-extended-key-event-message

At the moment, it looks like this in filter:

`vnc.qemu.key_event.down_flag == True`

`vnc.qemu.key_event.down_flag == False`

And on the screen:

![image](/uploads/f752ac8de9d1b86685c99b6d7b9a29f9/image.png){width=264 height=48}

![image](/uploads/dae4efa95f0250e7812a5a4b5ade592e/image.png){width=263 height=45}

I'd welcome better names, though.
I think True and False are fine here.
Need to replace BASE_NONE by length of flag

changed this line in [version 5 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19287/diffs?diff_id=1295239493&start_sha=6351dd5a181dfd2319d067811aec04308b35dead#cfc6b5284483868ee3ac2b54fc662eba573887b5_4281_4281)

I'm sorry but I can't really understand what for should I do that. If I replace `BASE_NONE by length of the flag` I receive a linter error:

```
Error: epan/dissectors/packet-vnc.c hf_vnc_qemu_extended_key_down_flag type is FT_BOOLEAN, no mask set ( 0x0 ) - display should be BASE_NONE, is instead 2
```

I don't think that any mask is to be imposed because the specification unambiguously states:
```
Down-flag is non-zero (true) if the key is now pressed, zero (false) if it is now released.
```

See: https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#keyevent

So, it doesn't matter what bit is set. Additionally, I see a lot if usage FT_BOOLEAN without the flag length.

Am I missing something?

@alagoutte, @martin.r.mathieson As far as I can see, there are two possible options:

**1)**

```
		{ &hf_vnc_share_desktop_flag,
		  { "Share desktop flag", "vnc.share_desktop_flag",
		    FT_BOOLEAN, BASE_NONE, NULL, 0x0,
		    "Client's desire to share the server's desktop with other clients", HFILL }
		},
```

which produces graphical representation:

![image](/uploads/fd33954acbafd16bf692e06287bae3c8/image.png){width="193" height="33"}

and the filter

```
vnc.share_desktop_flag == True
```

**2)**

```
		{ &hf_vnc_auth_result,
		  { "Authentication result", "vnc.auth_result",
		    FT_BOOLEAN, 32, TFS(&auth_result_tfs), 0x1,
		    NULL, HFILL }
		},
```

producing

![image](/uploads/39bf6f40e9dd4dbca0873204ddc1c62f/image.png){width="430" height="30"}

with filter

```
vnc.auth_result == False
```

I strongly support the first option and I'm really don't want to use the second one. Reasons are:

* The second option explicitly points to a single bit in the flag which is not true in case of `down-flag` field.

  RFB Specification does not give a specific bit in 2-bytes field to test as a flag:

  ```
   Down-flag is non-zero (true) if the key is now pressed, zero (false) if it is now released. 
  ```

  See: https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#keyevent

  or

  See: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6143#section-7.5.4
* There are no specific flag names like

  ```
  static const true_false_string auth_result_tfs = {
  	"Failed",
  	"OK"
  };
  ```
* Filter expression doesn't match its' graphical representation. While from the graphic representation it should look like something "auth_result == OK", in reality it is

  ```
  vnc.auth_result == False
  ```

  By me, it is kinda unexpected and unclear behaviour.

Could you please share your thoughts about the possible options? Maybe there is a guide or something I don't know yet.

@alagoutte, @martin.r.mathieson, hello! Could you please give me some hints about correct boolean dissection in this particular case? 

I tried my best to describe the two possible options in there: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19287#note_2399161223
Option 1 is fine, John.

Thanks, @martin.r.mathieson .

Waiting for @alagoutte's confirmation or further requests.
Good for me too (i don't remember you can use FT_BOOLEAN with BASE_NONE :))
We're good to go, then.
